note: (continuation) 'ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles' — broader Isa 61 priest-people-vindicated background to the martyrs' reversal of the beast's persecution; the vindication of those who refused the mark.
sourceText: But you shall be named the priests of Yahweh; men will call you the ministers of our God: you will eat the wealth of the nations, and you will boast in their glory.

note: The slain in the vision 'lived, and stood up' (LXX ezēsan) — the resurrection-vivification verb 'they lived' (ezēsan) may echo the Ezekiel dry-bones revival; faint lexical parallel.
sourceText: So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up on their feet, an exceedingly great army.

note: 'set thy face against Gog, the land of Magog' — the proper names 'Gog and Magog' are lifted directly from Ezekiel; Rev makes Magog a second figure rather than a land, but the verbal source is unmistakable. Hays volume/recurrence: explicit naming.
sourceText: Son of man, set your face toward Gog, of the land of Magog, the prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal, and prophesy against him,

note: Gog comes 'out of the north... a great company, and a mighty army... thou shalt come up against my people of Israel, as a cloud to cover the land' — source for the gathered host marching up against God's people. Coheres with 'went up over the width of the earth... surrounded the camp.'
sourceText: You shall come from your place out of the uttermost parts of the north, you, and many peoples with you, all of them riding on horses, a great company and a mighty army; and you shall come up against my people Israel, as a cloud to cover the land: it shall happen in the latter days, that I will bring you against my land, that the nations may know me, when I shall be sanctified in you, Gog, before their eyes.

note: 'I will rain upon him... fire and brimstone' (LXX pyr kai theion) — direct source of 'fire came down out of heaven... and devoured them' and of 'lake of fire and sulfur.' Strong lexical match (pyr/theion).
sourceText: With pestilence and with blood will I enter into judgment with him; and I will rain on him, and on his hordes, and on the many peoples who are with him, an overflowing shower, and great hailstones, fire, and sulfur.

note: 'I will send a fire on Magog' — reinforces the fire-from-God consuming Gog/Magog; recurrence with 38:22. Direct thematic and onomastic link.
sourceText: I will send a fire on Magog, and on those who dwell securely in the islands; and they shall know that I am Yahweh.

note: 'as the sand which is upon the sea shore' (LXX hōs hē ammos hē para to cheilos tēs thalassēs) — innumerable-as-the-sand idiom for the gathered army. Also Josh 11:4; 1 Sam 13:5 use it of hostile hosts; Hays: stock biblical idiom for countless multitude.
sourceText: that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your seed greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your seed will possess the gate of his enemies.

note: Gog brought 'upon the mountains of Israel' and destroyed there — the host's advance onto the holy land/people parallels surrounding the camp of the saints and the beloved city.
sourceText: and I will turn you around, and will lead you on, and will cause you to come up from the uttermost parts of the north; and I will bring you on the mountains of Israel; and I will strike your bow out of your left hand, and will cause your arrows to fall out of your right hand. You shall fall on the mountains of Israel, you, and all your hordes, and the peoples who are with you: I will give you to the ravenous birds of every sort, and to the animals of the […]

note: 'I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle' — the eschatological gathering of the nations to war against the holy city undergirds 'gather them together to the war' and 'the beloved city.' Hays coherence with the Zech siege motif.
sourceText: For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city will be taken, the houses rifled, and the women ravished. Half of the city will go out into captivity, and the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.

note: Jerusalem made 'a cup of trembling' and 'a burdensome stone' against which 'all the people of the earth be gathered' — siege of the city by all nations, then their destruction; parallels the surrounding-then-consumed pattern.
sourceText: “Behold, I will make Jerusalem a cup of reeling to all the surrounding peoples, and on Judah also will it be in the siege against Jerusalem. It will happen in that day, that I will make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all the peoples. All who burden themselves with it will be severely wounded, and all the nations of the earth will be gathered together against it.

note: 'let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee' (LXX katabēsetai pyr ek tou ouranou) — closest lexical parallel for 'fire came down out of heaven... and devoured them'; Hays volume on the exact phrase though the Ezek 38–39 context is primary.
sourceText: Elijah answered to the captain of fifty, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from the sky, and consume you and your fifty!” Fire came down from the sky, and consumed him and his fifty.

note: 'The LORD loveth the gates of Zion' — possible background to 'the beloved city' (tēn polin tēn ēgapēmenēn) as the city God loves; faint, the epithet may be Rev's own coinage.
sourceText: Yahweh loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.

note: The invader who 'march[es] through the breadth of the land' (LXX poreuomenon epi ta platē tēs gēs) — close lexical parallel to 'went up over the width of the earth (epi to platos tēs gēs).'
sourceText: For, behold, I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, that march through the breadth of the earth, to possess dwelling places that are not theirs.

note: Topheth prepared, 'the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone (theion), doth kindle it' — source for the fiery lake of burning/brimstone into which the devil is thrown; provides the burning-pile-of-fire-and-brimstone image.
sourceText: For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, for the king it is prepared. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. Yahweh’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.

note: 'their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched' — the unending torment of the condemned ('tormented day and night forever and ever') resonates with the unquenchable fire of Isaiah's final verse.
sourceText: “They shall go out, and look on the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they will be loathsome to all mankind.”

note: Oath 'by him that liveth for ever' (eis ton aiōna) — the 'forever and ever' eternity formula has Danielic resonance, though it is a stock LXX/Rev liturgical phrase.
sourceText: I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand to heaven, and swore by him who lives forever that it shall be for a time, times, and a half; and when they have made an end of breaking in pieces the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.

note: 'the judgment was set, and the books were opened' (LXX/Theod. kritērion ekathisen, kai bibloi ēneōchthēsan) — direct source for 'they opened books' and judgment before the throne. Hays volume: the opened-books-of-judgment is distinctively Danielic.
sourceText: A fiery stream issued and came out from before him: thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.

note: 'his throne was like the fiery flame... the Ancient of days did sit' — the enthroned judge whose throne dominates the scene; source for 'a great white throne, and him who sat on it.' Whiteness draws on the Ancient of Days' garment 'white as snow.'
sourceText: I saw until thrones were placed, and one who was ancient of days sat: his clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.

note: 'every one that shall be found written in the book' delivered, and the dead 'awake... some to everlasting life, and some to... everlasting contempt' — the book-enrollment determining destiny and the resurrection-to-judgment of all the dead. Source for the book of life deciding the lake of fire.
sourceText: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book. Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

note: The smashed image elements blown away 'and no place was found for them' (LXX kai topos ouch heurethē autois) — near-verbatim source of 'There was found no place for them' (topos ouch heurethē autois). Strong lexical match.
sourceText: Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken in pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshing floors; and the wind carried them away, so that no place was found for them: and the stone that struck the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.

note: 'Let them be blotted out of the book of the living (LXX biblou zōntōn)... not be written with the righteous' — the book of life from which names are absent; source for being judged by enrollment / 'not found written in the book of life.'
sourceText: Let them be blotted out of the book of life, and not be written with the righteous.

note: 'blot me out of thy book which thou hast written... whosoever hath sinned... will I blot out of my book' — the divine register of the living/saved; foundational for the book-of-life motif alongside Ps 69:28.
sourceText: Yet now, if you will, forgive their sin—and if not, please blot me out of your book which you have written.” Yahweh said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.

note: 'I the LORD search the heart... to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings' — direct source of the recurring 'judged... according to their works / according to his works.' Hays recurrence with Ps 62:12; Rev 2:23; 22:12.
sourceText: I, Yahweh, search the mind, I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.

note: 'thou renderest to every man according to his work' (LXX kata ta erga autou) — closest lexical parallel to 'each one according to his works'; reinforces Jer 17:10 as the judged-by-works topos.
sourceText: Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work.

note: 'it is written before me... I will recompense, even recompense into their bosom' — the written record before God grounding judgment by deeds; parallels the books of works opened in judgment.
sourceText: “Behold, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will recompense, yes, I will recompense into their bosom,

note: 'The sea saw it, and fled' (LXX hē thalassa... ephygen) — the fleeing of sea/earth before God; lexical resonance with earth and heaven that 'fled away' (ephygen) from the throne. Hays: theophanic flight of creation.
sourceText: The sea saw it, and fled. The Jordan was driven back.

note: 'Tremble, thou earth, at the presence of the Lord' — creation's terrified retreat before God's face; coheres with earth/heaven fleeing from his face.
sourceText: Tremble, you earth, at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the God of Jacob,

note: 'I will ransom them from the power of the grave (Sheol/Hades); I will redeem them from death: O death... O grave (LXX hadē), I will be thy destruction' — source for Death and Hades surrendering the dead and then being destroyed (thrown into the lake of fire). Hays: the personified Death/Hades pairing.
sourceText: I will ransom them from the power of Sheol. I will redeem them from death! Death, where are your plagues? Sheol, where is your destruction? “Compassion will be hidden from my eyes.

note: 'He will swallow up death in victory' (LXX katepien ho thanatos ischysas) — the abolition of Death itself; source for Death being thrown into the lake of fire / the second death. Coheres with 1 Cor 15:54-55.
sourceText: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.

note: 'shame and everlasting contempt' for the resurrected wicked — the 'second death' as the negative resurrection outcome; reinforces the two-destiny judgment of all the dead.
sourceText: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

note: 'the earth shall cast out the dead (LXX hē gē tōn asebōn peseitai / dead shall arise)' — resurrection of the dead from the earth; faint background to land/sea/Hades giving up their dead.
sourceText: Your dead shall live. My dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will cast out the departed spirits.

note: 'the earth shall give back that which has been entrusted to it, and Sheol... shall give back that which it owes' — Second-Temple parallel to 'the sea gave up the dead... Death and Hades gave up the dead.' Strong conceptual match for the universal resurrection-disgorging of the realms of the dead.
sourceText: [source text not in the World English Bible]

note: Sheol/the chambers of souls restoring the dead at the consummation — Second-Temple background to the realms of the dead releasing their dead for judgment.
sourceText: [source text not in the World English Bible]

note: Verbal and thematic core: 'new heavens and a new earth' (LXX ouranos kainos kai ge kaine) with the 'former things not remembered/passed away' motif — John's 'new heaven and a new earth' and 'the first things have passed away' (v.4) draws on both halves. Strongest availability and recurrence; Hays' volume and thematic coherence both high.
sourceText: “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.

note: Doublet of 65:17: 'the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me' — reinforces the eschatological permanence theme. Together with 65:17 establishes the dominant intertext.
sourceText: “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me,” says Yahweh, “so your seed and your name shall remain.

note: 'He will wipe away every tear' (v.4) echoes 'the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces' and 'he will swallow up death forever' — joint source for tear-wiping and death's abolition. MT 'swallow up death' vs LXX 'death prevailed having swallowed' diverges; John follows the death-abolished sense (cf. MT / Theodotion). High volume.
sourceText: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.

note: Covenant-dwelling formula: 'My dwelling place (LXX kataskenosis) will be with them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people' — directly behind v.3 ('God's dwelling is with people... they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God'). Recurrence with Lev 26 strengthens.
sourceText: My tent also shall be with them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

note: Foundational covenant formula: 'I will set my tabernacle/dwelling among you... I will walk among you and be your God, and you shall be my people.' Source of the Ezek 37:27 reuse; Revelation's plural 'peoples' (laoi, best text) universalizes the singular covenant 'people.'
sourceText: I will set my tent among you, and my soul won’t abhor you. I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.

note: 'I will dwell in the midst of you... and many nations shall join themselves to the LORD... and shall be my people' — supports v.3's expanded 'peoples' and the God-dwelling-with-humanity theme; verbal contact with the dwelling formula.
sourceText: Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion; for, behold, I come, and I will dwell in your midst,’ says Yahweh. Many nations shall join themselves to Yahweh in that day, and shall be my people; and I will dwell in your midst, and you shall know that Yahweh of Armies has sent me to you.

note: 'Awake, awake... O Jerusalem, the holy city; put on your beautiful garments' — behind the 'holy city' title (v.2) and the adornment imagery; recurs at 21:27 ('nothing unclean shall enter').
sourceText: Awake, awake, put on your strength, Zion; put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean.

note: Bridal-adornment simile (v.2): 'as a bridegroom decks himself... and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels' — close conceptual and verbal match for 'prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.'
sourceText: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.

note: Zion as bride married to God: 'as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride... so shall your God rejoice over you'; the city given a new name. Supports the New Jerusalem-as-bride identification.
sourceText: For Zion’s sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until her righteousness go out as brightness, and her salvation as a lamp that burns. The nations shall see your righteousness, and all kings your glory, and you shall be called by a new name, which the mouth of Yahweh shall name. You shall also be a crown of beauty in the hand of Yahweh, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God. You shall no more be termed Forsaken; […]

note: 'Sorrow and sighing shall flee away' parallels 'no more mourning, nor crying, nor pain' (v.4); paired with 51:11. Thematic coherence high though verbal contact diffuse.
sourceText: The Yahweh’s ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.”

note: Doublet of 35:10 ('sorrow and sighing shall flee away'); reinforces the abolition-of-grief catalogue in v.4.
sourceText: The ransomed of Yahweh shall return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy shall be on their heads. They shall obtain gladness and joy. Sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

note: 'They shall be my people and I will be their God' — another instance of the covenant formula feeding v.3; faint given many parallel attestations.
sourceText: and I will bring them, and they will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and they will be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.”

note: 'I will say... You are my people, and they shall say, You are my God' — covenant-formula reuse; low independent weight beside Lev 26 / Ezek 37.
sourceText: I will sow her to me in the earth; and I will have mercy on her who had not obtained mercy; and I will tell those who were not my people, ‘You are my people;’ and they will say, ‘My God!’”

note: The 'peoples' (laoi) who serve in the everlasting kingdom may color the plural in v.3; faint and contested.
sourceText: There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.

note: 'New heaven and a new earth' as deliberate recreation of the Gen 1 'heavens and the earth' — figural new-creation framing; structurally cued but verbally generic.
sourceText: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

note: 'Remember not the former things' — paired with 43:19 (next pericope); supports 'the first/former things have passed away' (v.4).
sourceText: “Don’t remember the former things, and don’t consider the things of old.

note: 'Am I the sea?' / the sea as chaos-monster domain may underlie 'the sea is no more' (v.1); part of the OT chaos-sea / Leviathan complex.
sourceText: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?

note: The 'great sea' from which the beasts arise — 'the sea is no more' (v.1) as the elimination of the source of chaos/the beast (cf. Rev 13:1). Figural; contested.
sourceText: Daniel spoke and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the sky broke out on the great sea. Four great animals came up from the sea, diverse one from another.

note: 'Behold, I am making all things new' (v.5) draws on 'Behold, I am doing a new thing' (idou ego poio kaina, LXX) — the 'behold... new' formula. High verbal contact with the LXX of Isa 43:19.
sourceText: Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.

note: 'I will give freely (dorean) to him who is thirsty from the spring of the water of life' (v.6) echoes 'Ho, every one who thirsts, come to the waters... without money' — free gift to the thirsty. Verbal ('thirsty,' 'freely/without price') and thematic match.
sourceText: “Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.

note: 'I am the first, and I am the last' underlies 'the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End' (v.6); recurs at Rev 1:8,17; 22:13. Cf. also Isa 41:4; 48:12 for the same self-predication.
sourceText: This is what Yahweh, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies, says: “I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God.

note: 'I will be his father, and he shall be my son' — Davidic adoption formula directly behind 'I will be his God, and he will be my son' (v.7). Revelation democratizes the royal promise to every overcomer.
sourceText: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men;

note: Davidic sonship: 'He shall cry to me, You are my Father, my God... I will make him the firstborn' — reinforces 2 Sam 7:14 behind v.7; royal-firstborn coloring.
sourceText: He will call to me, ‘You are my Father, my God, and the rock of my salvation!’ I will also appoint him my firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.

note: 'I am the first, I also am the last' — doublet of 44:6 supporting the Alpha-Omega self-designation (v.6).
sourceText: “Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.

note: 'Living waters shall flow out from Jerusalem' supports 'the spring of the water of life' (v.6); fully developed in Rev 22:1. Thematic coherence high.
sourceText: It will happen in that day, that living waters will go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the eastern sea, and half of them toward the western sea; in summer and in winter will it be.

note: 'With you is the fountain of life' — direct verbal source for 'the spring of the water of life' (v.6); pege zoes in LXX.
sourceText: For with you is the spring of life. In your light shall we see light.

note: 'The fountain of living waters' (God) contrasted with broken cisterns — colors the 'spring of the water of life' (v.6).
sourceText: “For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of living waters, and cut them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.

note: 'Springs of water will guide them' for the redeemed who 'will not hunger or thirst' — feeds the thirst/spring motif (v.6); also echoed in Rev 7:16-17.
sourceText: They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun strike them: for he who has mercy on them will lead them, even by springs of water he will guide them.

note: 'Fire and sulfur (brimstone)' raining on Sodom (v.8 'fire and sulfur') — the canonical brimstone-judgment image. Cf. Ezek 38:22; Ps 11:6.
sourceText: Then Yahweh rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah sulfur and fire from Yahweh out of the sky.

note: 'Everyone whose name is written in the book' — undergirds the overcomer/inheritance contrast with the excluded (v.7-8) and the book-of-life of v.27.
sourceText: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.

note: 'Fire and sulfur' rained in judgment on Gog — reinforces the 'lake that burns with fire and sulfur' (v.8).
sourceText: With pestilence and with blood will I enter into judgment with him; and I will rain on him, and on his hordes, and on the many peoples who are with him, an overflowing shower, and great hailstones, fire, and sulfur.

note: 'He carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the holy city' (v.10) closely reproduces Ezekiel's visionary transport: 'he brought me... and set me upon a very high mountain, on which was the frame of a city.' Tour-of-the-city framework derives directly from Ezek 40-48.
sourceText: In the visions of God brought he me into the land of Israel, and set me down on a very high mountain, whereon was as it were the frame of a city on the south.

note: Twelve gates inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes, three on each of the four sides (v.12-13), reproduces Ezekiel's gate-list (three N, three E, three S, three W, named for the tribes). Highest structural and verbal correspondence for the gates.
sourceText: These are the exits of the city: On the north side four thousand and five hundred reeds by measure; and the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel, three gates northward: the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; the gate of Levi, one. At the east side four thousand and five hundred reeds, and three gates: even the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; the gate of Dan, one. At the south side four thousand and […]

note: Bridal imagery resumed (v.9 'the wife, the Lamb's bride') — cf. 21:2; the bride 'adorned' theme carries into the jewel-glory description (v.11).
sourceText: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.

note: 'Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you' underlies 'having the glory of God. Her light was like a most precious stone' (v.11). Isa 60 is the controlling intertext for the city's radiance and is quarried throughout 21:23-26.
sourceText: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory is risen on you. For, behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples; but Yahweh will arise on you, and his glory shall be seen on you.

note: 'The glory of the God of Israel... the earth shone with his glory' as it enters the temple-city — parallels the city 'having the glory of God' (v.11). Reinforces the Ezekielian glory-filling pattern.
sourceText: Behold, the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east: and his voice was like the sound of many waters; and the earth shined with his glory. It was according to the appearance of the vision which I saw, even according to the vision that I saw when I came to destroy the city; and the visions were like the vision that I saw by the river Chebar; and I fell on my face. Yahweh’s glory came into the house by the way of the gate whose prospect is […]

note: Jerusalem rebuilt with sapphires, jewels, and precious-stone gates — anticipates the jasper radiance (v.11) and is the chief source for the foundations/gates jewelry developed in 21:18-21.
sourceText: “You afflicted, tossed with storms, and not comforted, behold, I will set your stones in beautiful colors, and lay your foundations with sapphires. I will make your pinnacles of rubies, and your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.

note: The high priest's breastpiece bearing the names of the twelve tribes engraved on twelve stones (v.12 'names of the twelve tribes') — links the tribe-inscribed gates to priestly typology; develops fully at 21:19-20.
sourceText: The stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, everyone according to his name, they shall be for the twelve tribes.

note: The wilderness camp arranged by tribes three-per-side around the tabernacle on the four compass points — pattern behind the three-gates-per-side arrangement (v.13).
sourceText: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying, “The children of Israel shall encamp every man by his own standard, with the banners of their fathers’ houses: at a distance from the Tent of Meeting shall they encamp around it.” Those who encamp on the east side toward the sunrise shall be of the standard of the camp of Judah, according to their divisions: and the prince of the children of Judah shall be Nahshon the son of Amminadab. His division, and those […]

note: The wall surrounding the temple-complex measured by the angel — anticipates the 'great and high wall' (v.12) and the measuring of 21:15-17.
sourceText: Behold, a wall on the outside of the house all around, and in the man’s hand a measuring reed six cubits long, of a cubit and a hand breadth each: so he measured the thickness of the building, one reed; and the height, one reed.

note: The angelic man with 'a measuring reed' who measures the temple-city (v.15 'a golden reed to measure the city') reproduces Ezekiel's measuring-tour guide. Recurs through Ezek 40-42.
sourceText: He brought me there; and, behold, there was a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of brass, with a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed; and he stood in the gate.

note: The holy district/city given equal square measurements on its four sides — source for 'the city is square, and its length is as great as its width' (v.16). Cf. Ezek 45:1-3 for the foursquare holy portion.
sourceText: These shall be its measures: the north side four thousand and five hundred, and the south side four thousand and five hundred, and on the east side four thousand and five hundred, and the west side four thousand and five hundred.

note: The inner sanctuary (Holy of Holies) a perfect cube ('twenty cubits long, twenty wide, twenty high') overlaid with gold — behind 'its length, width, and height are equal' (v.16) and the all-gold city (v.18): the whole city is the Most Holy Place. Strong typological coherence.
sourceText: Within the oracle was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in breadth, and twenty cubits in its height; and he overlaid it with pure gold: and he covered the altar with cedar.

note: 'I will lay your foundations with sapphires... your gates of carbuncles, and all your border of precious stones' — the principal OT source for the jewel-adorned foundations and pearl-like gates (v.19-21). LXX of 54:12 has the gates of crystal/stones.
sourceText: “You afflicted, tossed with storms, and not comforted, behold, I will set your stones in beautiful colors, and lay your foundations with sapphires. I will make your pinnacles of rubies, and your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.

note: The twelve stones of the high priest's breastpiece (v.19-20 jewel list) — the foundations' twelve gems correspond to the priestly stones, though John's order/LXX equivalences differ. High volume; flag LXX (Exod 28:17-20 LXX) as John's likely stone-name source.
sourceText: You shall set in it settings of stones, four rows of stones: a row of ruby, topaz, and beryl shall be the first row; and the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald; and the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst; and the fourth row a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper: they shall be enclosed in gold in their settings.

note: The man with a measuring line going to measure Jerusalem — parallels the measuring of the city (v.15-16); paired with Ezek 40.
sourceText: I lifted up my eyes, and saw, and behold, a man with a measuring line in his hand. Then I asked, “Where are you going?” He said to me, “To measure Jerusalem, to see what is its breadth and what is its length.”

note: The square 'holy portion' set apart with the sanctuary in it — undergirds the foursquare, sanctified dimensions of the city (v.16).
sourceText: Moreover, when you shall divide by lot the land for inheritance, you shall offer an offering to Yahweh, a holy portion of the land; the length shall be the length of twenty-five thousand reeds, and the breadth shall be ten thousand: it shall be holy in all its border all around. Of this there shall be a five hundred by five hundred square for the holy place; and fifty cubits for its suburbs all around. Of this measure you shall measure a length of […]

note: The temple's pure gold furnishings — contributes to the 'pure gold, like pure glass' city/street imagery (v.18,21).
sourceText: and the cups, and the snuffers, and the basins, and the spoons, and the fire pans, of pure gold; and the hinges, both for the doors of the inner house, the most holy place, and for the doors of the house, of the temple, of gold.

note: Second-Temple parallel: New Jerusalem 'built with sapphires and emeralds... your walls and towers and battlements with pure gold... the streets of Jerusalem with beryl and ruby and stones of Ophir' — strikingly close to v.18-21 (gold, gems, jeweled streets). Likely shared exegetical tradition on Isa 54.
sourceText: For Jerusalem will be built with sapphires, emeralds, and precious stones; your walls and towers and battlements with pure gold. The streets of Jerusalem will be paved with beryl, carbuncle, and stones of Ophir.

note: 'For bronze I will bring gold' — the eschatological upgrade of building materials feeds the all-gold city (v.18,21).
sourceText: For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron. I will also make your officers peace, and righteousness your ruler.

note: The made breastpiece stones (parallel list to Exod 28) — secondary attestation of the twelve-stone priestly source for v.19-20.
sourceText: They set in it four rows of stones. A row of ruby, topaz, and beryl was the first row; and the second row, a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald; and the third row, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst; and the fourth row, a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper. They were enclosed in gold settings. The stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, everyone according to his […]

note: 'The sun shall be no more your light by day... but the LORD will be your everlasting light' — direct source for 'the city has no need for the sun, neither of the moon... the very glory of God illuminated it' (v.23). Highest verbal and thematic correspondence in the pericope.
sourceText: The sun shall be no more your light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light to you: but Yahweh will be to you an everlasting light, and your God your glory. Your sun shall no more go down, neither shall your moon withdraw itself; for Yahweh will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning shall be ended.

note: 'Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising' underlies 'the nations will walk in its light. The kings of the earth bring...' (v.24). Isa 60 is the controlling text for v.23-26.
sourceText: Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising.

note: 'Your gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day or night, that men may bring to you the wealth of the nations' — direct source for 'its gates will in no way be shut' and the bringing-in of the nations' glory (v.25-26).
sourceText: Your gates also shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring to you the wealth of the nations, and their kings led captive.

note: 'The wealth/abundance of the nations shall come to you' — supports 'the glory and honor of the nations' brought into the city (v.24,26).
sourceText: Then you shall see and be radiant, and your heart shall thrill and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be turned to you, the wealth of the nations shall come to you.

note: The city's name 'The LORD is there' (YHWH-shammah) — God's unmediated presence stands behind 'no temple... for the Lord God... and the Lamb are its temple' (v.22).
sourceText: It shall be eighteen thousand reeds around: and the name of the city from that day shall be, Yahweh is there.

note: 'A unique day... not day and not night, but at evening time there shall be light' — source for the perpetual-light / 'no night there' motif (v.23,25). Cf. Zech 14:6 (no cold/frost) and 14:8 (living waters).
sourceText: It will be a unique day which is known to Yahweh; not day, and not night; but it will come to pass, that at evening time there will be light.

note: 'There shall no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean' underlies 'there will in no way enter into it anything profane' (v.27); the holy city's purity-boundary.
sourceText: Awake, awake, put on your strength, Zion; put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean.

note: 'No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart or flesh, shall enter my sanctuary' — purity-exclusion source for v.27; pairs with Isa 52:1.
sourceText: Thus says the Lord Yahweh, No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into my sanctuary, of any foreigners who are among the children of Israel.

note: The Holy Way on which 'the unclean shall not pass over it' — supports the exclusion of the profane/unclean (v.27).
sourceText: A highway will be there, a road, and it will be called The Holy Way. The unclean shall not pass over it, but it will be for those who walk in the Way. Wicked fools will not go there.

note: 'Let them be blotted out of the book of the living' — the negative counterpart behind 'only those who are written in the Lamb's book of life' (v.27). Cf. Exod 32:32-33; Dan 12:1.
sourceText: Let them be blotted out of the book of life, and not be written with the righteous.

note: 'Jerusalem shall dwell in security, there shall be no more curse/ban' — supports the secure, unbarred-gates and no-defilement picture (v.25,27); fully echoed at Rev 22:3.
sourceText: Men will dwell therein, and there will be no more curse; but Jerusalem will dwell safely.

note: The destruction of the covering/veil over the nations on the mountain — undergirds the unmediated divine presence ('no temple,' v.22) and the nations' inclusion.
sourceText: He will destroy in this mountain the surface of the covering that covers all peoples, and the veil that is spread over all nations. He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.

note: 'Everyone whose name shall be found written in the book' shall be delivered — parallel to the Lamb's book of life (v.27); also undergirds Rev 13:8; 20:15.
sourceText: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.

note: 'The treasures/desire of all nations shall come, and I will fill this house with glory' — possible coloring of the nations bringing their glory into the temple-city (v.24,26).
sourceText: and I will shake all nations. The precious things of all nations will come, and I will fill this house with glory, says Yahweh of Armies.

note: Kings bringing tribute and all nations serving — royal-homage background to 'the kings of the earth bring the glory and honor of the nations' (v.24).
sourceText: The kings of Tarshish and of the islands will bring tribute. The kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts. Yes, all kings shall fall down before him. All nations shall serve him.

note: The temple-river flowing out from under the threshold, with fruit trees on both banks bearing fresh fruit monthly and leaves for healing, is the dominant structural model for the river + tree(s) + monthly fruit + healing-leaves cluster. Volume and recurrence both very strong (Hays). LXX and Hebrew agree closely on the healing-leaves motif (Ezek 47:12).
sourceText: He brought me back to the door of the house; and behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward; (for the forefront of the house was toward the east;) and the waters came down from under, from the right side of the house, on the south of the altar. Then he brought me out by the way of the gate northward, and led me round by the way outside to the outer gate, by the way of the gate that looks toward the east; and behold, there ran […]

note: The tree of life in Eden's midst and the river going out of Eden to water the garden. Eschaton-as-restored-Eden; thematic coherence and recurrence with Gen 3 are decisive. 'In the middle of its street' echoes the tree 'in the middle of the garden' (Gen 2:9).
sourceText: Out of the ground Yahweh God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became the source of four rivers.

note: Reversal of the expulsion: access to the tree of life, barred by the cherubim and flaming sword, is now restored to the servants (cf. 22:14). The 'no more curse' note ties directly back to the Eden judgment. Strong figural reversal.
sourceText: Yahweh God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he reach out his hand, and also take of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...” Therefore Yahweh God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken. So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim/f + cherubim are powerful angelic creatures, messengers of God with wings. See Ezekiel 10./f* at the east of the garden of […]

note: Living waters going out from Jerusalem feeds the 'water of life' image; Zech 14 is a recurring matrix for Rev 21–22 (see also 14:7, 14:11). Coherence with Ezekiel's temple-river tradition.
sourceText: It will happen in that day, that living waters will go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the eastern sea, and half of them toward the western sea; in summer and in winter will it be.

note: 'There shall be no more curse/utter destruction (cherem); Jerusalem shall dwell securely.' Direct verbal-thematic source for 'There will be no curse any more.' Hebrew cherem (devoted-to-destruction); LXX renders anathema — Rev's katathema is closer to the LXX register.
sourceText: Men will dwell therein, and there will be no more curse; but Jerusalem will dwell safely.

note: No sun or moon for light, for the LORD will be everlasting light. Direct source for 'no night... no lamp... the Lord God will illuminate them.' Coherence with Rev 21:23. LXX and Hebrew agree.
sourceText: The sun shall be no more your light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light to you: but Yahweh will be to you an everlasting light, and your God your glory.

note: The saints of the Most High receive and possess the kingdom; ground of 'they will reign forever and ever.' Coherence with Rev 5:10, 20:4. Aramaic/OG both attest eternal reign of the holy ones.
sourceText: But the saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom forever, even forever and ever.

note: The kingdom and dominion given to the people of the saints of the Most High, an everlasting kingdom — reinforces the reign motif. Closely paired with 7:18.
sourceText: The kingdom and the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole sky, shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High: his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.

note: Aaronic blessing: the LORD make his face shine upon you, and his name put upon the people of Israel. Strong conceptual pairing for 'see his face' + 'his name on their foreheads.' The name-bestowal of v.27 is the key link; coherence with Rev 3:12, 14:1.
sourceText: Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’ “So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.”

note: 'I shall behold your face in righteousness; I shall be satisfied when I awake with your likeness.' Beatific-vision source for 'They will see his face.' LXX Ps 16:15.
sourceText: As for me, I shall see your face in righteousness. I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with seeing your form.

note: 'When shall I come and appear before God / see the face of God?' Thirst-for-the-vision motif; fainter, conceptual. LXX Ps 41:3 reads 'see the face of God' where MT has 'appear before.' Flag LXX vs Hebrew divergence.
sourceText: My soul thirsts for God, for the living God. When shall I come and appear before God?

note: A unique day, not day and not night, but at evening time there shall be light. Underlies 'no night... the Lord God will illuminate them' alongside Isa 60:19. Coherence within the Zech 14 matrix.
sourceText: It will be a unique day which is known to Yahweh; not day, and not night; but it will come to pass, that at evening time there will be light.

note: 'A river whose streams make glad the city of God.' River-in-the-city image feeds the throne-river flowing through the street; thematic coherence. LXX Ps 45:5.
sourceText: There is a river, the streams of which make the city of God glad, the holy place of the tents of the Most High.

note: 'The LORD is there' (YHWH-shammah) as the city's name; faint support for the divine presence/illumination and name-bearing themes climaxing the new Jerusalem.
sourceText: It shall be eighteen thousand reeds around: and the name of the city from that day shall be, Yahweh is there.

note: A fountain coming forth from the house of the LORD, watering the valley — a parallel temple-river tradition reinforcing Ezek 47 / Zech 14. Faint, contested as direct source.
sourceText: It will happen in that day, that the mountains will drop down sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, all the brooks of Judah will flow with waters, and a fountain will flow out from Yahweh’s house, and will water the valley of Shittim.

note: 'He will swallow up death forever' — broader curse-removal / no-more-tears matrix behind 'no more curse'; faint here, stronger at Rev 21:4.
sourceText: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.

note: 'There is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known... what will be in the latter days / what must happen.' Source for the apocalyptic formula 'the things which must happen soon' (with Dan 2:29, 2:45). Rev 1:1 and 22:6 frame the book by this Danielic idiom.
sourceText: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these:

note: 'O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh.' Title source for 'the Lord God of the spirits of the prophets' (Rev adapts 'of all flesh' to 'of the prophets'). Coherence with Num 27:16.
sourceText: They fell on their faces, and said, “God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and will you be angry with all the congregation?”

note: 'Let the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, set a man over the congregation.' Parallel divine title behind 'the God of the spirits of the prophets.' Paired with Num 16:22.
sourceText: “Let Yahweh, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation,

note: 'Behold, the Lord GOD comes... his reward is with him.' The coming-with-recompense formula introduced here ('Behold, I come quickly') is fully developed in 22:12; Isa 40:10 is its base text. LXX and Hebrew agree on misthos/reward.
sourceText: Behold, the Lord Yahweh will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.

note: 'Seal up the vision, for it pertains to many days hence' — inverted at Rev 22:10 ('don't seal') and resonant with 'the time is at hand'; here the 'faithful and true / soon' framing sets up that contrast. Faint at this pericope.
sourceText: The vision of the evenings and mornings which has been told is true: but seal up the vision; for it belongs to many days to come.

note: Daniel falls before the angelic interpreter (cf. 10:9). Background for John falling to worship the revealing angel, though the prohibition of angel-worship is distinctive to Rev. Faint, generic.
sourceText: So he came near where I stood; and when he came, I was frightened, and fell on my face: but he said to me, Understand, son of man; for the vision belongs to the time of the end.

note: 'Many shall purify themselves... but the wicked shall act wickedly; and none of the wicked shall understand, but the wise shall understand.' Direct source for the let-the-unjust-remain-unjust / let-the-righteous-remain-righteous antithesis. Strong volume and verbal echo (esp. OG/Theodotion).
sourceText: Many shall purify themselves, and make themselves white, and be refined; but the wicked shall do wickedly; and none of the wicked shall understand; but those who are wise shall understand.

note: 'Shut up the words, and seal the book, until the time of the end' — pointedly REVERSED by 'Don't seal up the words... for the time is at hand.' Programmatic inversion (with Dan 12:9). Hays: recurrence + thematic coherence high.
sourceText: But you, Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run back and forth, and knowledge shall be increased.”

note: 'I am the first and I am the last; besides me there is no god.' Direct source for 'the First and the Last' (and the Alpha–Omega equivalent). Near-quotation of a divine self-identification applied to the risen Lord. LXX and Hebrew agree.
sourceText: This is what Yahweh, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies, says: “I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God.

note: 'I am he; I am the first, and I am the last.' Second base text for 'the First and the Last.' Paired with Isa 44:6; coherence with Rev 1:17, 21:6.
sourceText: “Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.

note: 'I, the LORD, the first, and with the last, I am he' — third witness to the first/last self-predication, calling the generations from the beginning. Reinforces 22:13.
sourceText: Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, Yahweh, the first, and with the last, I am he.”

note: 'Will he not repay each according to his work?' Direct source for 'to repay to each man according to his work.' Strong verbal correspondence (kata ta erga). LXX agrees.
sourceText: If you say, “Behold, we didn’t know this”; doesn’t he who weighs the hearts consider it? He who keeps your soul, doesn’t he know it? Shall he not render to every man according to his work?

note: 'You repay each according to his work.' Parallel source for the recompense-by-works formula (Ps 61:13 LXX). Often cited jointly with Prov 24:12 in NT (cf. Rom 2:6).
sourceText: Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work.

note: 'Behold, the Lord GOD comes... his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.' Direct source for 'My reward is with me.' LXX and Hebrew agree (misthos).
sourceText: Behold, the Lord Yahweh will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.

note: 'Behold, your salvation comes; behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.' Twin to Isa 40:10 behind 'My reward is with me, to repay each.' Coherence strong.
sourceText: Behold, Yahweh has proclaimed to the end of the earth, “Say to the daughter of Zion, ‘Behold, your salvation comes. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.’”

note: 'I the LORD search the heart... to give to each according to his ways, according to the fruit of his deeds.' Reinforces recompense-by-works; thematic, slightly fainter than Prov/Ps.
sourceText: I, Yahweh, search the mind, I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.

note: 'Repay them according to their work / the work of their hands.' Another recompense-by-deeds source (Ps 27:4 LXX); conceptual, paired with Prov 24:12.
sourceText: Give them according to their work, and according to the wickedness of their doings. Give them according to the operation of their hands. Bring back on them what they deserve.

note: 'The words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.' Restates 12:4; sharpens the reversal at Rev 22:10. Coherence within the Daniel-sealing motif.
sourceText: He said, Go your way, Daniel; for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.

note: 'The vision is yet for the appointed time... it will surely come, it will not delay' — supports 'the time is at hand' / 'I come quickly.' Faint, conceptual.
sourceText: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
lxxText: For the vision is yet for a time, and it shall shoot forth at the end, and not in vain: though he should tarry, wait for him; for he will surely come, and will not tarry.

note: 'The day of the LORD is at hand' — generic 'time/day is near' idiom behind 'the time is at hand.' Common prophetic formula, not a single source.
sourceText: Wail; for the day of Yahweh is at hand! It will come as destruction from the Almighty.

note: Right to the tree of life and entry restored — direct reversal of the barred access after Eden's expulsion. Coherence with 22:2; the 'right to the tree of life' is the Edenic inheritance regranted.
sourceText: Yahweh God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he reach out his hand, and also take of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...” Therefore Yahweh God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken. So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim/f + cherubim are powerful angelic creatures, messengers of God with wings. See Ezekiel 10./f* at the east of the garden of […]

note: 'A shoot from the stump of Jesse, a branch from his roots.' Source for 'the root... of David.' Davidic-messianic root imagery; coherence with Rev 5:5. LXX 'rhiza' matches 'root.'
sourceText: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.

note: 'The root of Jesse, who shall stand as a signal to the peoples; him shall the nations seek.' Direct source for 'the root... of David' as the messianic ensign; LXX explicit 'rhiza tou Iessai.'
sourceText: It will happen in that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.

note: Balaam: 'a star shall come out of Jacob, a scepter shall rise out of Israel.' Source for 'the Bright and Morning Star' as messianic title. Strong messianic-star tradition (also at Qumran); coherence with Rev 2:28.
sourceText: I see him, but not now. I see him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob. A scepter will rise out of Israel, and shall strike through the corners of Moab, and break down all the sons of Sheth.

note: 'Everyone who thirsts, come to the waters... without money and without price.' Direct source for 'He who is thirsty, let him come... take the water of life freely (dorean).' Strong verbal + thematic. LXX dorean matches.
sourceText: “Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.

note: 'Come, let us walk in the light of the LORD' — invitation-to-come framing; faint background to the threefold 'Come!' Generic invitation idiom.
sourceText: House of Jacob, come, and let us walk in the light of Yahweh.

note: 'Dogs' excluded from the assembly (the 'wages of a dog' barred from the house of the LORD) — possible background for 'Outside are the dogs.' Conceptual; the metaphor is debated.
sourceText: You shall not bring the hire of a prostitute, or the wages of a male prostitute, into the house of Yahweh your God for any vow; for both of these are an abomination to Yahweh your God.

note: 'Open to me the gates of righteousness... this is the gate of the LORD; the righteous shall enter through it.' Faint background for the righteous entering by the gates into the city. Conceptual.
sourceText: Open to me the gates of righteousness. I will enter into them. I will give thanks to Yah. This is the gate of Yahweh; the righteous will enter into it.

note: 'Open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faith may enter in.' Reinforces the gates-entry-of-the-righteous motif behind 'enter in by the gates into the city.' Faint.
sourceText: Open the gates, that the righteous nation may enter: the one which keeps faith.

note: 'You shall not add to the word which I command you, nor take from it.' Direct source for the add/take-away canonical-formula warning. Strong verbal correspondence (prostithemi / aphaireo). LXX and Hebrew agree.
sourceText: You shall not add to the word which I command you, neither shall you take away from it, that you may keep the commandments of Yahweh your God which I command you.

note: 'Whatever I command you... you shall not add to it nor take from it.' (Deut 13:1 in MT/LXX.) Twin to Deut 4:2 behind the don't-add / don't-take-away warning. Coherence high.
sourceText: Whatever thing I command you, that you shall observe to do. You shall not add to it, nor take away from it.

note: 'Do not add to his words, lest he rebuke you and you be found a liar.' Direct source — the 'add to his words' + threatened penalty pattern matches 'if anyone adds... may God add the plagues.' LXX agrees.
sourceText: Don’t you add to his words, lest he reprove you, and you be found a liar.

note: 'I will bring more plagues upon you, sevenfold for your sins' — covenant-curse 'add plagues' formula behind 'may God add to him the plagues.' Coherence with the Exodus-plagues motif in Rev 15–16. LXX plege.
sourceText: “‘If you walk contrary to me, and won’t listen to me, then I will bring seven times more plagues on you according to your sins.

note: 'The LORD will blot out his name... and all the curses written in this book will fall on him.' Background for 'may God take away his part... which are written in this book' (blotting / written-curses). Coherence with the Deuteronomic curse tradition.
sourceText: Yahweh will not pardon him, but then Yahweh’s anger and his jealousy will smoke against that man, and all of the curse that is written in this book will fall on him, and Yahweh will blot out his name from under the sky.

note: 'Whoever has sinned against me, I will blot out of my book.' Faint background for taking away one's 'part from the tree of life' / removal from the book/city (book-of-life motif). Conceptual.
sourceText: Yahweh said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.

note: Deliverance for those 'found written in the book' — faint support for the inscribed-in/erased-from-the-city-and-life motif behind the take-away penalty. Faint.
sourceText: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
